label: Circles
overview: Circle questions on the SAT cover arc length, sector area, central angles, inscribed angles, and the equation of a circle in the coordinate plane. The key relationships: a central angle equals its arc in degrees; an inscribed angle equals half its arc. The standard equation (x−h)² + (y−k)² = r² has centre (h, k) and radius r.

workedExamples.problem: A circle has equation x² + y² − 6x + 4y = 12. Find the centre and radius.

steps.title: Complete the square for x
steps.content: Group x terms: x² − 6x. Add (−6/2)² = 9 to both sides.

steps.title: Complete the square for y
steps.content: Group y terms: y² + 4y. Add (4/2)² = 4 to both sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading the centre of (x−3)² + (y+2)² = 25 as (−3, 2) instead of (3, −2)
commonMistakes.fix: The standard form is (x−h)² + (y−k)². Match signs carefully: (x−3) means h = 3; (y+2) = (y−(−2)) means k = −2.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing arc length with arc measure (degrees)
commonMistakes.fix: Arc measure is the central angle in degrees. Arc length is the actual distance along the curve — it depends on both the angle and the radius.

quickTip: Whenever you see a circle equation not in standard form, complete the square immediately. The SAT frequently tests whether students can recognise a circle equation that needs rearranging.
